Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we can size the right deployment mode for Acme:

What we heard
- Latency target: p95 <= 50ms for user-facing recommendation calls (short responses, ~15-40 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~500 req/s during peak windows, with bursts to ~1.2k req/s for up to 90s
- Multi-region: primary traffic US with some EU reads; data residency not a blocker today
- Constraint: procurement wants a clear plan for predictable costs and SLA for the holiday peak

Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoff (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest path to production, simple auth & SDKs, built-in autoscaling and burst capacity. Good if you can accept some variability in p95 under sustained, very high throughput.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and lower p95 at high sustained qps. Better when you need strict latency SLOs and cost predictability.

Attachments: I attached your latency spreadsheet (acme_latency_requirements.xlsx) and our Dedicated pricing brief — feel free to share with procurement.

Next steps
1) Dev deep dive: schedule a 60-min technical sizing with Dev (cc'd) to go over exact token sizes, model choices, and traffic shape — can you share a 1-week traffic sample (CSV) and typical prompt lengths?
2) We'll run a quick hosted vs dedicated projection (latency/ops cost) and return an initial recommendation + config.
3) Procurement: we'll prepare a short TCO sheet and an example dedicated commitment term once you confirm volumes.

Proposed times for the technical session: Thu 26 Feb 10:00-11:00 PT or Mon 2 Mar 09:00-10:00 PT. Which works best?

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the data points. A few technical notes ahead of Thursday's session to help you prep and for your procurement folks:

1) Latency expectations
- Hosted API: for short payloads (~15–40 tokens) and modest sustained traffic, p95 is typically in the 45–80ms range depending on model selection and region. Hosted benefits from our multi-tenant autoscaler but under sustained high qps p95 can increase due to scheduling/burst shaping.
- Dedicated: with reserved GPU pools and dedicated batching parameters, we've seen p95 in the 25–40ms range for the same model family at 500+ sustained qps. Dedicated also gives you control over batch size and concurrency tradeoffs.

2) Throughput and burst handling
- If bursts are short (<=120s) and average remains ~500 qps, Hosted can absorb bursts using burst capacity, but cost may spike. If you need guaranteed headroom without cost variability, Dedicated with burst buffer options is preferable.

3) Migration path
- It's standard to start on Hosted and then migrate to Dedicated. Migration steps: pin a model version, coordinate a cutover window (usually low-traffic hour), switch DNS/route rules or update client endpoint, and verify KV cache warm-up. Downtime is typically minimal (<5 minutes) if warmed in advance; we also support a parallel warm-up traffic pattern to eliminate user impact.

4) Configuration suggestions
- Initial Dedicated recommendation: 2 x medium dedicated pools (autoscale range 2–6) with a reserved baseline to hit 500 qps and 30% burst buffer. We'll propose an exact GPU class and slot count after we see the traffic CSV and token histogram.

I've attached the Dedicated pricing brief (redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf) and a short latency benchmarking note. For Thu, please include a sample of your 1-minute per-second qps profile and a typical prompt token distribution.

Cheers,
